**Ben David Alford** (born December 20, 1964) is an American actor, [playwright](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Playwright "Playwright"), and author, best known for portraying Bucky Dawes on the television series _[Nashville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nashville\_(2012\_TV\_series) "Nashville (2012 TV series)")_.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=David_Alford&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Alford was born and raised in [Adams, Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adams,_Tennessee "Adams, Tennessee") on his family's farm.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Alford#cite_note-1) His parents were Ben Robert Alford, a minister, and Sheridan (Durham). Alford attended [Jo Byrns High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Byrns_High_School "Jo Byrns High School") in nearby [Cedar Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cedar_Hill,_Tennessee "Cedar Hill, Tennessee"), and then went for two years to [Martin Methodist College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Methodist_College "Martin Methodist College") in [Pulaski](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulaski,_Tennessee "Pulaski, Tennessee"). He next transferred to [Austin Peay State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austin_Peay_State_University "Austin Peay State University") in [Clarksville, Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clarksville,_Tennessee "Clarksville, Tennessee"). At APSU he was originally a vocal performance major, but switched to the theatre program.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Alford#cite_note-:0-2)

## Acting

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=David_Alford&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Acting")]

When playwright [Arthur Kopit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Kopit "Arthur Kopit") was visiting APSU as an artist in residence, he noticed Alford's acting talent and arranged for him to audition for the [Juilliard School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juilliard_School "Juilliard School") drama program. Alford did so, and was accepted to the program.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Alford#cite_note-3)

After spending a few years in [New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City") upon graduation from Juilliard, Alford moved back to Tennessee and founded Mockingbird Theatre in [Nashville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nashville,_Tennessee "Nashville, Tennessee"). He was artistic director of this theatre from 1994 to 2004, when he accepted the position of artistic director for [Tennessee Repertory Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nashville_Repertory_Theatre "Nashville Repertory Theatre").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Alford#cite_note-4) He held this position until 2007, but spent an additional year at Tennessee Rep as an artist-in-residence.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Alford#cite_note-5)

In 2012 Alford joined the cast of the television series _Nashville_, portraying Bucky Dawes, the manager of country music star Rayna Jaymes ([Connie Britton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connie_Britton "Connie Britton")).[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Alford#cite_note-6) Alford appeared on the show until it ended in 2018.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Alford#cite_note-7)

In 2017 Alford appeared in the [Broadway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadway_theatre "Broadway theatre") revival of _[The Little Foxes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Little\_Foxes "The Little Foxes")_ with [Laura Linney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Linney "Laura Linney"), [Cynthia Nixon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cynthia_Nixon "Cynthia Nixon"), [Michael McKean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_McKean "Michael McKean"), and [Richard Thomas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Thomas_(actor) "Richard Thomas (actor)"). Alford portrayed Mr. Marshall, as well as understudying McKean and Thomas.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Alford#cite_note-8)

## Writing

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=David_Alford&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Writing")]

Alford has written two plays that are presented annually as part of the Bell Witch Fall Festival in his hometown of Adams.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Alford#cite_note-:0-2)_Spirit: The Authentic Story of the Bell Witch of Tennessee_ (2002) recounts the [Bell Witch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bell_Witch "Bell Witch") legend. _Smoke: A Ballad of the Night Riders_ (2010) is set against the [Black Patch Tobacco Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Patch_Tobacco_Wars "Black Patch Tobacco Wars").

Alford also co-authored the book _Living the Dream: The Morning After Drama School_ with Brian Horner.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Alford#cite_note-9)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=David_Alford&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Alford has two children from his first marriage. Since the fall of 2018, he has been a visiting artist in residence at [Berry College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berry_College "Berry College") in [Mount Berry, Georgia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Berry,_Georgia "Mount Berry, Georgia").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Alford#cite_note-10)
